record.original_question: Classify Proper Holomorphic Correspondences from the unit disc to itself.

evidence.quote: Problem 9.3.1 Classify Proper Holomorphic Correspondences from the unit disc to itself.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Delta = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| < 1\}$ denote the open unit disc. A proper holomorphic correspondence from $\Delta$ to $\Delta$ is an irreducible complex-analytic subvariety $V \subset \Delta \times \Delta$ of pure dimension $1$ such that both coordinate projections $\pi_1, \pi_2 : V \to \Delta$ are proper surjective holomorphic maps with finite fibers. Two such correspondences $V, V' \subset \Delta \times \Delta$ are considered equivalent if there exist automorphisms $\varphi, \psi \in \mathrm{Aut}(\Delta)$ such that $(\varphi \times \psi)(V) = V'$.

Classify, up to this equivalence, all proper holomorphic correspondences from $\Delta$ to itself.
artifact.status_search_result: A search did not return a definitive classification of proper holomorphic correspondences from the unit disc to itself. While proper holomorphic maps and automorphisms of the disc are well-understood (Möbius transformations, finite Blaschke products in the case of finite-sheeted proper maps), no authoritative source confirming a complete classification of proper holomorphic correspondences $\Delta \to \Delta$ was located, so the current status is unclear.

status_evidence.title: Holomorphic maps of the unit disc (UCSD lecture notes)
status_evidence.snippet: Schwarz's Lemma and characterizations of holomorphic self-maps of the unit disc.
status_evidence.claim: Proper holomorphic self-maps of the disc are classically known (finite Blaschke products), but no analogous classification of correspondences was located.

status_evidence.title: Proper holomorphic discs in C^2
status_evidence.snippet: Studies proper holomorphic maps from the unit disc but not correspondences from disc to disc.
status_evidence.claim: Related literature addresses proper holomorphic maps from the disc but not a classification of disc-to-disc correspondences.
